hints: Notice the three given frequencies increase from P at $3 \times 10^{10} \text{ Hz}$ to Q at $3 \times 10^{13} \text{ Hz}$ to R at $6 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$, so their spectrum regions must be in increasing frequency order.
Recall that visible light has frequency around $4$ to $7 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$, so compare R at $6 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$ with that band first.

Use $\lambda = c/f$ with $c = 3.0 \times 10^{8} \text{ m s}^{-1}$ to check P and Q: P gives about $10^{-2} \text{ m}$ and Q gives about $10^{-5} \text{ m}$, then match these wavelengths to microwave and infra-red.
walkthrough: List the given data: P is $3 \times 10^{10} \text{ Hz}$, Q is $3 \times 10^{13} \text{ Hz}$, R is $6 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$, so frequency increases P < Q < R.
Recall the electromagnetic spectrum in order of increasing frequency: radio, microwave, infra-red, visible, ultraviolet, X-ray, gamma ray.
Check R first because it is most distinctive: visible light is about $4 \times 10^{14}$ to $7 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$, so $6 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$ lies inside the visible band.

Check Q: $3 \times 10^{13} \text{ Hz}$ is below visible but above microwave. Using $\lambda = c/f = 3.0 \times 10^{8} / 3 \times 10^{13} = 1 \times 10^{-5} \text{ m}$, which is $10 \text{ } \mu\text{m}$, a typical infra-red wavelength.

Check P: $3 \times 10^{10} \text{ Hz}$ is lower still. Using $\lambda = c/f = 3.0 \times 10^{8} / 3 \times 10^{10} = 1 \times 10^{-2} \text{ m}$, which is $1 \text{ cm}$, a typical microwave wavelength.
Therefore P is microwave, Q is infra-red and R is visible. This is option B.

A.explanation: Frequencies of $3 \times 10^{10} \text{ Hz}$ and $3 \times 10^{13} \text{ Hz}$ are too low for infra-red and visible light.

B.explanation: Increasing frequency $3 \times 10^{10} \text{ Hz}$ to $6 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$ matches the order microwave, then infra-red, then visible.

C.explanation: Ultraviolet, X-ray and gamma ray all need frequencies above about $10^{15} \text{ Hz}$, much higher than P, Q and R.

D.explanation: Visible light is near $4$ to $7 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$, so only R at $6 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$ can be visible, not P.
